existing_baseline.description: Programmatic 144x144 indexed PNG, 4-frame subtle head-bob idle animation, 40px humanoid silhouette drawn from home palette indices BG=0 / LEG=4 / BODY=6 / HEAD=10. Generated by synth_sheet.py (T-0198). This is what the spike would have compared against.
existing_baseline.note: Visual inspection of the synthetic sheet at 40px confirms the silhouette shape reads and the head-bob is detectable. This is the bar any SDXL-generated output must clear.

generation_recipe_ready.descent: box-average 1152->144 then palette-quantize to home_palette.json (Oklab, dithering OFF)
generation_recipe_ready.controlnet_required: ControlNet pose grid mandatory — without it, SDXL returns frontal concept-art studies, not animation frames (documented in T-0209 and T-0218 story)
generation_recipe_ready.reference_conditioning: T-0209 concept sheet (player_character_concept_sheet_v1.png, concept_hash=4f82e3c42dbc0d4ba6960144f6507c5d6dbd7fb0945c54558532d922c9c0251b) as IP-Adapter input

decision: NOT_RUN — defaulting to deterministic synthesis per the documented fallback rule (T-0218 card: 'ambiguous ⇒ default to the script'). NOT_RUN is treated as the ambiguous case since generation quality was never evaluated. Deterministic synthesis (synth_sheet.py / synth_entities.py pattern, already proven in T-0200 / T-0214) remains the active approach for character sheets until WSL→ComfyUI access is unblocked and a real spike can run.
unblock_path: Option A: approve curl or node tool calls in the automated runner's permission model for this worktree, then re-run T-0218. The recipe and reference assets are ready. Option B: run MANUAL_GENERATION.md on the Windows host side, descend the output, and attach the result directly to this card — the 4-question evaluation can then be done by a human with the image in hand.

four_question_framework_for_re_run.q1_silhouette_readable_at_40px: Does the figure read as a distinct human shape when the 1152px output is box-averaged to 144px (the sheet), then a single 48px cell is cropped and displayed at 40px figure height? Squint test: cover 90% of the sheet and check the remaining area still reads.
four_question_framework_for_re_run.q2_identity_holds_across_frames: Do adjacent idle frames (cells 0,0 → 0,1 → 0,2 → 1,0) show the same character, or does the head/torso geometry drift enough that a player would notice? 1px head-drift is the documented failure threshold.
four_question_framework_for_re_run.q3_beats_synthetic_at_game_scale: Placed side-by-side in a 384x216 game room with the 40px synthetic sheet, does the SDXL-descended version offer a visible quality improvement in silhouette clarity or animation smoothness? If not, the synthetic is cheaper and reproducible with no loss.
four_question_framework_for_re_run.q4_failure_mode: If the sheet fails q1 or q2, classify: (a) wrong subject — the model generated something other than the intended character (corpus / IP-Adapter conditioning problem); (b) mush at 40px — the character reads at 1152px but detail is destroyed by descent (descent problem, §6.13 escalation: retrain LoRA on palette-quantized data); (c) identity drift — frame-to-frame inconsistency (generation problem, requires per-frame img2img seeding or more ControlNet weight).
